conviction_note: Evidence roughly offsets: a primary-document supply skew toward late Q3/Q4 (servers) plus October PC CPU price hikes point to a firm Q4 guide, against a -20% Q3 PC unit market, a consensus already above the Q3 guide midpoint with a Q4 guide of ~$17.5B being talked up, and a name that sold a large beat-and-raise by 7.9% in July; impact_sum +0.30 and impact_scaled +0.2 agree that the sign is near a coin flip while the move itself should be large (implied ~9.2-9.4%, last four reactions 0.3/17.0/23.6/7.9).
bar: Q3 2026 revenue consensus $16.49B and non-GAAP EPS $0.40 (TradingKey citing Theta Research as of 2026-10-27, https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/262245484-inter-intc-ai-dcai-q3-tradingkey ; TipRanks $16.5B / $0.40, https://www.tipranks.com/news/intel-stock-analysts-take-on-intc-ahead-of-todays-earnings), against company guide $15.8-16.8B, 42.0% non-GAAP GM, $0.38 non-GAAP EPS (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000050863/000005086326000155/q226earningsrelease.htm). Q4 consensus about $16.9B revenue / $0.43 EPS per Wedbush, which itself expects a Q4 guide of $17.5B / $0.49 (TipRanks, 2026-10-29). Two agreeing estimate sources plus a company guide, so the bar is sourced. The stock trades on the Q4 guide, gross margin and foundry/capex commentary more than the reported quarter.
positioning_check: Short interest about 121.0M shares, ~2.9% of float, 1.1-1.2 days to cover at the 2026-07-15 FINRA settlement (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/intc/short-interest/ ; equibles 2.86% of float, 1.1 days, https://equibles.com/stocks/intc/shortinterest); no October settlement found. Not a crowded short. The sealed baseline failed (bars_failed: HTTPError), so there is no sealed spot, implied move or skew; third-party implied move ±9.2% as of 2026-10-28 (https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/intc-earnings-october-2026) and ±9.4% per TipRanks (https://www.tipranks.com/news/intel-q3-earnings-tomorrow-options-traders-expect-a-9-4-move-in-intc-stock). Skew not found. Price context: close $93.74 on 2026-10-27 (+3.6% that day), stock up ~150% YTD but well off its summer high (~$128 per TIKR, https://www.tikr.com/blog/intel-stock-is-up-126-this-year-its-already-given-back-a-third-of-its-gains); TipRanks reported it ~3% lower pre-market on 2026-10-29.

findings.finding: Intel's own Q2 prepared remarks say supply growth is 'more skewed towards the end of Q3 and into Q4, especially for servers', that demand still outstrips supply after wafer output beat plan, and that server CPU unit growth is forecast 'strong double-digit' this year and next; with DCAI at $6.3B (+59% YoY, +24% QoQ) in Q2, this sets up a Q4 guide above the ~$16.9B Q4 consensus (Wedbush already looks for $17.5B).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide-driven: Apr 2026 +23.6% (beat and strong outlook); Jan 2026 -17.0% on a supply-constrained weak guide; Jul 2026 -7.9% despite a $1.8B revenue beat and a Q3 guide above the $15.0B consensus (earnings-watcher table). The guide line moves this stock by double digits in both directions.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus Q4 revenue of ~$16.9B is only ~3.5% above the Q3 midpoint, which is a normal seasonal step, not one that prices in the extra server supply Intel said would land late Q3 and in Q4. If it were priced, the consensus would sit near the $17.5B Wedbush expects and the stock would not be ~25% below its summer high.
findings.independence: TSMC on 2026-10-15 beat its Q3 guide (HPC +22% QoQ) and guided Q4 to $52.3-54.3B, calling AI demand 'extremely robust' (https://futurumgroup.com/?p=96944); server CPU lead times about six months and prices up as much as 20% since March (https://www.tomshardware.com/pc-components/cpus/shifting-need-for-cpus-in-ai-workloads-drives-intensifying-shortages-price-hikes). Both are proxies, not Intel numbers.

findings.finding: IDC's preliminary Q3 2026 data have worldwide PC shipments down 20.1% YoY to 62.7M units and down 9.1% QoQ, with HP -30.9%, Dell -25.0% and Lenovo -22.6%, and IDC expects consumer demand to keep declining with channels worried about excess inventory. That is a sharp unit drop for CCPG ($8.9B, ~55% of Intel Products revenue in Q2) going into the Q4 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In July Intel guided H2 PC consumption sub-seasonal and 2026 down low double digits; the stock fell 7.9% on that print, though the drop was not attributed to PC alone. In Jan 2026 (-17.0%) supply constraints on client were part of the weak guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The data have been public for three weeks, and Bernstein models -20-22% PC units and still expects $16.6B revenue. Intel already guided H2 PC as sub-seasonal, so this sits largely inside the guide. What is left is the channel-inventory risk for Q4 CCPG (HP -31%), which no preview quantifies. Sized net of DCAI (+59% YoY) and Intel's ability to shift wafers to servers.
findings.independence: TSMC (2026-10-15) said consumer markets face headwinds from rising component prices (https://futurumgroup.com/?p=96944); Wedbush and Bernstein both cite weak PC demand and memory costs as limiting the beat (https://www.tipranks.com/news/intel-stock-analysts-take-on-intc-ahead-of-todays-earnings).

findings.finding: DigiTimes reported (via MobileSyrup, 2026-09-08) that Intel planned a second ~10% PC CPU price increase for early October 2026, explicitly choosing margin over share, and that Intel may cut 5-10% of its workforce. Together these support Q4 ASP/gross margin and non-GAAP opex in the guide, at the cost of possible restructuring charges below the line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 non-GAAP GM beat guide by ~280bp partly on 'pricing actions', and the stock still fell 7.9%, so margin upside alone has not been paid for recently.
findings.why_not_priced: The report is unconfirmed by Intel and few previews mention it. The Q4 consensus GM/EPS step (EPS $0.40 to $0.43) is modest, which would be larger if a 10% client price increase were modelled in.
findings.independence: DigiTimes-based reports of the October hike (https://www.club386.com/?p=155964); Intel's Q2 remarks credit Q2 GM upside to 'higher ASPs due to mix and pricing actions' (https://download.intel.com/newsroom/2026/earnings/Intel-Q22026-Earnings-Call.pdf). These share the DigiTimes origin for the October part.

findings.finding: KeyBanc-linked channel checks reported 2026-10-17 claim 14A/foundry volume wins at Broadcom, Google, Microsoft and Nvidia and say Apple is evaluating 14A for M/A-series. Intel has not confirmed any of them, and the 2026-10-29 call is billed as the test. External foundry revenue was only $293M in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Unconfirmed foundry customer reports have moved the stock up between prints (June 2026 Google/Nvidia reports; 2024 Amazon win +8% after hours). On print days Intel has not historically named new 14A customers.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced as expectation, not as fact. Average target $117.71 with a $200 high, and the stock rose 3.6% on 2026-10-27. The asymmetry is that a call silent on names (Intel's usual practice) would undercut a story the market has been handed, while a named customer would be a large positive. If the market had fully discounted silence, the run-up into the print would not have happened.
findings.independence: Intel's own remarks report 'increasing momentum on customer engagements for Intel 14A' and PDK 0.9 due in October (https://download.intel.com/newsroom/2026/earnings/Intel-Q22026-Earnings-Call.pdf), which supports engagement but not named contracts.

findings.finding: The bar has moved above Intel's own guide. Q3 consensus is $16.49B and $0.40 against a $16.3B / $0.38 midpoint, Wedbush expects a $17.5B Q4 guide against a $16.9B consensus, and Wedbush notes seven straight guidance beats. In July Intel beat its midpoint by $1.8B, guided Q3 above the $15.0B consensus, and the stock still fell 7.9%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beat-and-raise sold: Jul 2026 -7.9% and Jul 2025 -8.5%. Oct 2025 +0.3% on a beat. Only Apr 2026 (+23.6%) paid.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself. A beat is the expectation, so a beat within the typical $0.5-1.8B range is not news, and only a Q4 guide well above $17.5B or foundry specifics would clear the whisper. If the market expected only the published consensus, the beat history would show positive reactions on beats, and it does not.
findings.independence: Earnings-watcher reaction table (https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/intc-earnings-october-2026); TradingKey consensus vs guide midpoint (https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/262245484-inter-intc-ai-dcai-q3-tradingkey).

findings.finding: Intel raised a $15B underwritten equity offering on 2026-08-10 (plus a $2.25B option) for capex and working capital, and the July call guided 2027 capex 'significantly above' the >$20B 2026 level. That share-count dilution sits in Q3/Q4 EPS, and Wedbush says the reaction hinges partly on the 2027 investment commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Jul 2026: capex raised to >$20B together with a beat, and the stock fell 7.9%. Higher capex has not been rewarded on print days.
findings.why_not_priced: The raise itself is fully priced (August). What is open is the 2027 capex number. The money buys capacity for demand Intel says outruns supply, which TSMC's Q4 guide and six-month server CPU lead times corroborate. So the financing answer is 'funds a ramp', a zero rather than a negative, and only a capex figure far above expectations would move it.
findings.independence: Intel Q2 remarks on locking tool POs and substrates (https://download.intel.com/newsroom/2026/earnings/Intel-Q22026-Earnings-Call.pdf), the same company source as finding 1 but on a different line.

findings.finding: Q2 non-GAAP GM was 41.8%, ~280bp above guide on yields and pricing. Intel says 18A has cut Panther Lake's primary SKU cost ~50% YTD with another ~20% due this year, and Q3 18A yields were tracking ahead of March targets, which points to Q3 GM above the 42.0% guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 GM beat (+280bp) came with a -7.9% reaction, so this name has recently sold reported-quarter margin beats.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Consensus EPS of $0.40 vs the $0.38 guide implies only a small margin beat, while Bernstein's $0.49 shows how far upside could run. Rasgon flags 18A ramp costs as a margin headwind, so the street is not uniformly modelling GM upside.
findings.independence: Shares a document with finding 1 (different line). Bernstein's above-consensus EPS (https://www.tipranks.com/news/intel-stock-analysts-take-on-intc-ahead-of-todays-earnings).

outside_window.finding: Reported 14A customer contracts (Apple M/A-series, Terafab, Amazon) would become revenue-relevant only with 2027-2028 risk and HVM ramps; formal announcements may come later than the print.

baseline_tension: No sealed skew or run-up exists (baseline failed). Against the third-party context (stock +150% YTD but ~25% off its summer high, +3.6% on 10-27, beats sold in July), the evidence is two-sided and does not take a side against the market.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sold its July margin beat): the reported-quarter gross-margin finding cut from +1.0 to +0.5, and p_up moved from 52 to 51.

Rule 6 (inside what the company guided): the IDC PC finding cut from -1.0 to -0.7, because Intel had already guided H2 PC sub-seasonal; Rule 9 (net of the rest) applied in the same single cut, since DCAI growth and wafer reallocation offset client weakness.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the equity raise/capex finding kept at 0, because the money funds supply-constrained demand corroborated by TSMC and server lead times.
Rules 5 and 7: proxies kept as independence rather than separate findings; short interest checked (not crowded), so the negatives were not shrunk for squeeze risk. Every other finding left standing.
